title: Data Explore
summary: Keyboard-first explorer for a CSV or JSON dataset: a dense datagrid with per-column filters, two linked charts (each draws the grid's filtered rows; brush a range or a category and the grid and the other chart narrow to it), column stats, a Group By table that filters on click, undo history with presets, and a command palette (Cmd+K). Exports the filtered CSV and one PNG per chart. Pick it for any tabular data question: explore, slice, count, compare.

charts.description: Up to two charts, left to right. Each { type: bar|line|area|scatter|histogram (default bar), x: column (required), y?: number column (omit to count rows), series?: column (one group per value), aggregate?: count|sum|mean|min|max (default by type) }. Empty = two automatic charts: a bar of the first category with 2-50 values (split by a second category with 2-6), and a histogram of the first number column.

filters.description: Starting grid filters, { column: text } in datagrid syntax: 'ber' contains, '=Berlin' exact, '>5' '<=5' '2..9' for numbers, '2026-06..2026-08' for dates.

columns.description: Visible column ids in display order; every other column is hidden. Empty = all columns in file order.

sort.description: Starting sort, { id: column, dir: 'asc' | 'desc' }. Omit for file order.

pivot.description: Starting Group By table, { by: column, value: number column or null for row counts, agg: count|sum|mean|min|max }.

customScript.description: JS run last as (t3template, options) to bolt on controls, panels, buttons and presets. See boltOn.

controls.description: Starting values for bolt-on controls, { controlId: value }, applied when customScript adds them (a saved edit wins).

boltOn.summary: options.customScript runs once as new Function('t3template', 'options', code) after the dataset has loaded and the grid and charts exist. Read and drive the data through t3template.instances: grid (t3kit.datagrid: get, set, view, row, stats, select) and charts (t3kit.chart instances, one per chart, in order). Charts are linked: each draws the rows the grid's filters keep, except its own brush; the template manages chart rows, so change filters through the grid, not chart.set({ rows }). grid.set and chart.set are silent: call t3template.refresh() after them so the readouts, filter chips, stats and Group By table update. Every control edit is one undo step. Errors log '[t3template] customScript error: ...' and show in a dismissible banner. This is a data template (pipeline 'data'): addImageStage, addShaderStage, EDL hooks and addAudioFilter throw; bolt on through controls, panels, toolbar buttons, presets and the grid.
api: addControl({ id, label?, type: 'slider'|'toggle'|'select'|'color'|'text'|'button', min = 0, max = 1, step?, default?, options?: ['a', { value, label }], placeholder?, rows?, panel?: 'Title' | element from addPanel, onChange?(value, t3template), onClick?(t3template) }) -> { id, element, get(), set(value), setLabel(text) }. Values: slider number, toggle boolean, select the option value, color '#rrggbb', text string. No panel = 'Extras'. User edits run every hook and re-render; onChange runs on user edits only, not on load. Every control edit is one undo step.

addPanel(title | { title, open = true, position = 'top' }) -> the panel body element (append your own nodes; the same title returns the same panel). 'top' = after Active Filters and Column Stats, before Group By (first in view on load); 'bottom' = after History.

addToolbarButton(label, onClick(t3template), { shortcut?: 'shift+m' (any key not in reservedShortcuts), title? }) -> button (also listed in the command palette, Cmd+K).   refresh() re-renders the readouts, chips, stats and Group By table after silent grid or chart changes.

export() -> Promise<{ files: [{ name, type, size, width?, height? }] }>: the filtered CSV (visible columns, filtered rows) and one PNG per chart, sent to t3.workspace.attach and downloaded. The same as the Export button; it throws on failure.

getValues() -> { filters: { column: text }, sort: { id, dir } | null, charts: [{ type, x, y, series, aggregate }], pivot: { by, value, agg }, controls }.   setValues({ filters?, sort?, charts?, pivot? }, label?) -> Promise<values>: strict, so unknown keys and unknown columns throw. filters replaces the whole object; sort replaces; charts[i] merges into chart i (changing its x clears that chart's brush); pivot merges. One undo step.

addPreset(name, { filters?, sort?, charts?, pivot? }) / applyPreset(name): a preset is a full view, as setValues takes it. Presets and history steps also hold column order and brushes.   on('change', cb(values)) -> off.

instances: { grid (t3kit.datagrid; grid.get().filters is the live filter object, grid.view() the filtered source row indices, grid.match(filters) the rows any filter object keeps), charts (t3kit.chart instances, index 0 = first chart; a getter, so it follows dataset switches), history (t3kit.history) }.
